The family-wide contract for the **next-phase offer**: the guidance every pipeline command
surfaces at the end of its run, naming the natural next command(s). Cited by all pipeline
commands so the routing graph and the offer rules live in ONE place (the same shape as
`emit-block` in `feedback-emission.md`).

## The routing graph (role-aware)

**Every `/product-workflows:epics` option the routing graph names is conditional on the folder it names
holding an authored `prd.md`** (`kind: prd`): `/epics` accepts a PRD folder or an `EPIC-` folder
under one and refuses everything else (`/product-workflows:epics` Phase 0 step 1b). `/epics` also
stops while that `prd.md` is on no ref or only on an unmerged branch, and after a revision it stops
on the difference or reads the default branch's earlier copy, without the revision, until that
revision is merged (its Phase 0, *Gate the PRD*), so an offer of it by a run that has just written
or edited the PRD carries `<merge-clause>`. Where the
caller's PRD folder — the resolved folder itself on a PRD-level run, its parent on an Epic-level
one — holds no `prd.md`, which the BRD route reaches legitimately since `/product-workflows:create-prd`
is not a prerequisite for `/product-workflows:create-ard` there, the offer is
`/product-workflows:create-prd <PRD>` instead, `<PRD>` being that tested folder's own key and
never an Epic's — save where that folder holds the PRD under its pre-rename file name (the test
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/phase-handoff.md` §4.4's `prd.md` rung makes), on which
`/product-workflows:create-prd` would write a second PRD: there the offer names the rename, never
`/product-workflows:create-prd`, as §4.4's *The first missing document* names it, through
`/product-workflows:specify <PRD>`, whose own stop prints the rename's commands, saying that run
stops — **and only where `/product-workflows:create-prd` can itself run**: it refuses more than one shape —
three on the BRD route, and an `EPIC-` folder on either, which is why the key is the PRD folder's
— so on a BRD-route slice the slice's ledger tests are read first, and each offering command
names what `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/phase-handoff.md` §4.4's *The first missing document*
names for them at its `prd.md` rung, which restates them for a plugin that cannot read their
authority, `product-workflows:coverage-ledger-format` §5.2 — a naming, as that rung is, never a stop
that applies them, which is `/product-workflows:create-prd`'s own, taken in its Phase 0; and where they fail the offer resolves to what the
failing outcome names: `/product-workflows:brd-split` against one of two keys; no option at all
where none applies — the gate set non-empty and no row `covered-here`, the offer saying where the
requirements went, or the gate set empty and the parent's ledger unreadable, that ledger reported by
path; and, where the slice's `coverage-ledger.md` is missing or unreadable while `claims:` names
rows, no option either, the file reported by path and `/product-workflows:prd-ground <PRD>` named
beside the dropped option, in prose, never as an option or `(Recommended)`, as the run whose stop
tells an interrupted carve from a lost file and names the repair, saying it stops there by design.
Where the caller's PRD folder holds a `prd.md` asserting no `kind: prd`
— which `/epics` reads as no PRD and `/product-workflows:create-prd` counts as found, offering
`/product-workflows:update-prd` or an overwrite — the offer names neither: in their place it says
that the file asserts no `kind: prd`, and that adding the `kind: prd` and `key: <PRD>` its format
carries (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/addressing.md` §5) is what lets
`/product-workflows:epics <PRD>` read it, once that edit is merged to the default branch or, on a
specs tree that is no git repository, once it is made — where the offer is an option of a
question, the option left out and that said in the question's own text. An offer whose run stops the moment it starts is the same defect the
`<merge-clause>` rules exist to prevent, one command further on: a next step the operator
cannot take from the state the report describes.
